title: Specific characters are more variable than generic characters

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Specific characters are more variable than generic characters

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Characters that distinguish species within a genus are more variable within species than characters shared by all species of the genus, because the former have varied since the species branched from a common progenitor.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is notorious that specific characters are more variable than generic.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter V, “Laws of Variation”; section “Parts developed in an unusual manner are highly variable: specific characters more variable than generic: secondary sexual characters variable.”. Scope: species within genera of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch05-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variance comparison is feasible in clades with rich specimen sampling. Global tests are constrained by inconsistent character coding and sparse within-species replication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For traits used in taxonomy, compare within-species variation of species-diagnostic characters with genus-shared characters after scaling and measurement-error correction. Greater variation in specific characters supports the claim; equal or lower variation refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Taxonomists may choose stable diagnostic characters, creating ascertainment bias.

Generic and specific characters differ in measurement scale and type.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.76
discriminating power: 0.62
data existence: 0.67
analysis feasibility: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The comparison of variances is straightforward in birds, where individual measurements and generic placement are both public. It is partly circular if the traits are the ones systematists already picked as species differences, which is how the historical categories were built. A blind trait set can reduce that bias for birds and still leaves plants and most animals as a compilation project.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within genera, compare within-species variance of traits that differ among species with variance of traits shared across the genus, choosing the traits without using their diagnostic role. Greater variance of the species-level traits would confirm the claim; no difference under that blind choice would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Generic characters can be conservative by the way genera are diagnosed.

Characters used to distinguish species are often chosen because they vary.

TRY mostly stores species means, so within-species plant variances are sparse.

fields.label: Dimension scores

data existence: 0.58
